text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected for inference-gw-prod (us-west-2). 5xx spike > 10% over 5m. link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/2399212345 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall: @sasha (primary). Incident severity: sev2. Runbook: /runbooks/inference/5xx-spike.md

sasha: I'm on it. Starting triage — pulling logs and checking replicas.

kevin: saw this too from metrics dashboard. latency also climbing. tagging the recent rollout as potential cause.

sasha: quick snapshot:
```
ERROR infer-gw: handler failed to serve request id=abcd1234 status=502 kv_cache_miss=true backend_error=false
WARN autoscaler: pool-usw2-1 unready_replicas=2 pending_scale=3
```

sasha: looks like sudden cache miss cascade + insufficient warm pods. can we spin up a small scale or fallback to older routing?

emily: I can trigger a constrained scale up (reserved burst) — will do now. if unsuccessful, suggest re-routing to model-legacy-rt which has smaller memory footprint.

kevin: routing policy change would be faster than a full rollback. re-route 10% traffic first, then 50% if stable. want to avoid full rollback because of config churn.

sasha: agreed. rolling 10% -> 50% plan. I'll open the canary and watch KV hit rates.

incident-bot: action logged: canary_reroute started by sasha at 15:18 UTC.

sasha: FYI customer impact: embeddings and short-text generations degraded. Preliminary impact window ~15:02–15:35 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~8% of total for that window. No PII exposure.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff reminder in 30m to next oncall @emily.

kevin: we saw error rate drop to ~1.2% after 10% reroute. increasing to 50% now. monitoring for regression.

sasha: 50% reroute complete. KV miss rate stabilized, latency back to baseline. marking mitigation as successful. I'll start incident timeline notes.

on-system message: --- 40 minutes later ---

emily: taking over the thread for the second shift. congrats on quick mitigation. I'll keep an eye through end of shift and schedule postmortem.

emily: quick summary for handoff: root cause hypothesis — routing + autoscaler interplay caused temporary under-provisioning and amplified KV cache churn during a rollout. Mitigation: gradual reroute to legacy model variant, constrained scale-up fallback. Impact: elevated 5xx and tail latency for ~33 minutes; partial degradation for ~8% requests.

daniel: can we capture the exact rollout config that was active? I want to reproduce in staging.

kevin: yes — rollout id r-2026-03-15-89. config: continuous-balance policy with aggressive cold-start thresholds (threshold=0.3).

emily: OK scheduling postmortem. Proposed time: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. Please confirm availability. I'll create the doc and invite owners.

sasha: confirmed for 16:00 UTC. I'll own timeline and logs collection.

kevin: I'll own the root-cause writeup and model rollout config repro.

daniel: I'll take the action to add an e2e regression test for cold-starts to our CI.

emily: Action items (captured now):
- "runbook: update 5xx-spike.md steps to include canary-reroute and quick-scale checklist"  (owner: sasha, due: 2026-03-18)
- "alerts: add KV-miss alert and raise threshold for 1m -> 5m to avoid noisy pages" (owner: kevin, due: 2026-03-17)
- "deploy: add staged rollout guard (min-ready=2, max-step=20%) to prevent aggressive continuous-balance policies" (owner: eng-platform, contact: daniel, due: 2026-03-22)
- "tests: create e2e cold-start regression in staging and run on PRs touching rollout policy" (owner: daniel, due: 2026-03-19)
- "dashboards: surface per-model KV hit rate and cold-start rate in per-route dashboard" (owner: observability, contact: kevin, due: 2026-03-20)

emily: created postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood.internal/postmortems/2399212345-pager-multiplex-fallback (please add notes).

sasha: added initial timeline and log links to the doc. also attached small script to reproduce failing sequence in staging.

kevin: reminder: add runbook snippet for controlled rollback vs canary-reroute decision tree. small code block suggestion:
```
if kv_miss_rate > 0.2 and autoscaler_unready > 1:
  prefer canary_reroute()
else if rollout_traffic_change > 30%:
  consider immediate_rollback()
```

daniel: for accountability, let's add a periodic check on rollout policy metrics after each model push for 48h. owner: eng-platform.

emily: agreed. adding to action items.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 15:35 UTC; mitigation confirmed. Severity post-triage: sev2 -> sev3.

emily: final note: we'll review the runbook flow for simpler handoffs — include a one-line TL;DR at top with explicit next-step commands (reroute, scale, rollback) and who to page for each. sasha kevin daniel please add suggestions to the runbook before postmortem.

sasha: will do. tagging :spiral_note_pad:.

kevin: done. added suggested thresholds and links to dashboards.

emily: thanks all — postmortem invite + cal + doc in calendar. leaving monitoring to emily-night if anything pops off.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff complete. Next oncall: emily.

emily: closing thread for now. follow-ups will be tracked in the postmortem doc and the action-tracker board. :white_check_mark:
